title: Jest
description: All-in-one testing framework with mocking and coverage.

data.text: Jest is a zero-configuration testing framework. It includes an assertion library, mocking, and code coverage out of the box.

A Jest test lives in `describe` blocks that group related `it` or `test` cases. Matchers such as `toBe`, `toEqual`, and `toThrow` express the assertion. `beforeEach` and `afterEach` set up and tear down per test, and `setupFilesAfterEach` in the config registers global setup once.

data.title: Grouped tests with setup

data.text: `jest.mock` replaces a module with an auto-mock you can shape, `jest.fn` creates a spy, and `jest.useFakeTimers` makes time deterministic so a debounce or timeout does not slow the suite. Clearing mocks between tests prevents state leaking from one case to the next.

data.title: Mock a module and control timers
Interview angle: mock the boundary, not everything
data.text: The most common Jest mistake candidates describe is mocking so much that the test stops testing behavior. The strong answer is to mock only external boundaries — network, time, randomness, filesystem — and let pure logic run for real. Also mention `jest --coverage` and that a coverage number is a signal, not a goal.
